text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 triggered: Private interconnect instability in eu-west-2. Multiple BGP sessions to peer-exchange-52 are flapping; some customer routes (ACME Corp) withdrawn. Impact: private endpoints in eu-west-2 intermittently unreachable. Paging @anna.martinez (on-call).

anna.martinez: I'm on it — thanks. Can someone confirm scope: only ACME or other customers affected? Any known maintenance at the IX?

neteng-li: Quick check from our edge: BGP updates show repeated withdraws for prefix set 10.118.0.0/21 -> 10.118.7.255. Looks like route suppression at the IX. No scheduled maint.

devon.li: Seeing increased RPKI rejects on session to peer-exchange-52, maybe flapping path selection. Also observed spike in TCP retransmits on the interconnect.

sre-arnold: Customer reports TCP connections to private endpoints time out, app-level retries kick in. ACME confirmed they see ICMP unreachable to the remote overlay. They've opened a TAC with their provider as well.

anna.martinez: Runbook step 1: confirm BGP adj status and check our control-plane route table. Whoever has console access, paste `show bgp neighbors` and `show route table bgp | match 10.118`

neteng-li: Pasting sanitized output: ```
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcv MsgSent   TblVer  InQ OutQ Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
203.0.113.45    4 64512   3245   3221        0    0    0 00:12:34        0
203.0.113.46    4 64512   3246   3222        0    0    0 00:12:36        22
...
Routes for 10.118.0.0/21: withdrawn at 12:01:05, re-advertised 12:01:18, withdrawn 12:02:07
```

devon.li: That neighbor with 0 prefixes looks suspicious (203.0.113.45). Traceroute from our egress to the peer shows packet loss at `peer-ix-eu2-01` -> `peer-ix-eu2-02` hops.

anna.martinez: Possible ix fabric issue causing our session to drop. Mitigation plan: 1) attempt BGP session reset with peer 203.0.113.45 (coordinate with peer ops), 2) activate backup interconnect path for ACME (they have secondary advertised to eu-central-1), 3) temporary DNS failover to public fallback for customer private endpoint (if permitted).

customer-ops-jordan: ACME prefers private path; public fallback only as last resort. They authorized route failover to eu-central-1 pair earlier this quarter. They've given go for failover if it reduces customer impact.

infra-oncall: I'll coordinate the session reset. Devon, want me to trigger `clear bgp neighbor 203.0.113.45 soft` now?
devon.li: Do a soft reset first. Also capture tcpdump on the session for 60s: ```tcpdump -i ix0 host 203.0.113.45 and port 179 -w /tmp/bgp-203.0.113.45.pcap```

infra-oncall: Running soft reset now.

incident-bot: Note: oncall handoff scheduled at 1902348500 — if unresolved by then, paging will escalate to @devon.li per rotation.

neteng-li: After soft reset: neighbor 203.0.113.45 re-established, still showing intermittent withdraws though frequency reduced. pcap shows occasional TCP retransmit and 3-way handshake retries around seq retrans. Suspect transient packet loss in IX fabric.

anna.martinez: Okay, since soft reset only partially helped, step 2: we will fail ACME to their secondary interconnect in eu-central-1. Controlled failover plan: update outbound route preference (local-pref) to prefer routes via eu-central-1 for ACME prefixes, and ask ACME to steer traffic to secondary as well. This should be reversible.

devon.li: I'll prepare route-map change. Config diff: ```
route-map ACCME-OUT permit 10
 set local-preference 200
!
apply policy to vrf ACME outbound to peer 203.0.113.46
```

neteng-li: Pushing change now to a single edge (canary) to test.

anna.martinez: Monitor customer pings and our metrics. If we see drop in packet loss and application success, proceed with global change.

customer-ops-jordan: ACME reports initial improvement — some sessions now stable. They still see occasional resets for long-lived streams.

devon.li: Canary edge looks good, proceeding to apply to all active edges for ACME prefixes. Applying in 30s.

neteng-li: Rolled across all edges. Metrics: BGP withdraws for 10.118.0.0/21 down to zero, packet loss to ACME endpoints reduced from 6% -> 0.3%.

anna.martinez: :thumbsup: Good. Notify ACME that we've shifted them to secondary interconnect and ask them to validate application traffic. Also open a follow-up ticket to coordinate with IX provider to investigate fabric errors.

customer-ops-jordan: ACME confirms functionality restored for most flows. They will keep monitoring for 1 hour and report.

devon.li: Postmortem notes for now: root cause likely IX fabric induced packet loss causing BGP session instability and route suppression. Mitigation: route preference failover to secondary interconnect. Next steps: collect PCAPs, escalate to IX provider with timestamps and pcap, schedule maintenance window if provider needs physical intervention.

sre-arnold: Adding monitoring checks: create an alert for BGP neighbor prefix count drop > 50% in 5m for eu-west-2 peers and a synthetic probe from our edges to customer private endpoints to detect early regressions.

anna.martinez: Handoff note for next on-call (devon): issue mitigated by failover to eu-central-1 for ACME prefixes. Still open: provider investigation, PCAP analysis, and formal RCA. Please own follow-ups and coordinate with account team for customer communication.

devon.li: Acknowledged. I'll take post-incident ownership. Uploading PCAPs and configs to incident ticket INC-2026-452 and will ping IX ops with timeline + evidence.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 1902349050 (customer functional on secondary path). Continue post-incident actions in INC-2026-452.

anna.martinez: Closing slack loop here — if anything regresses ping @devon.li directly. Great work team. :coffee:
